analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and file metadata against the canonical definition index and selected T-041 detail. These changes affect CI review scheduling, spending and reporting, not provider encryption, attestation, authorization, cache isolation, billing-ledger operations or privileged fan control; no direct regression in the indexed runtime threats is established.
Bedrock workload mode raises the configurable native allowance to a bounded ceiling of 500 calls and defaults to larger output limits (.github/scripts/threat_review/bedrock.py:46-57). Stage planning reserves one shared repair slot and stops when the ceiling is exceeded (69-84); call-limit enforcement remains before fallback (114-128), and missing response accounting stops later requests (193-213). Increased bounded spending is explicit rather than an observed budget bypass.
The scanner now plans source and integration rounds, targets depth review to retained finding citations, substitutes Sol for overlapping Opus work, and preserves global integration uncertainty as a human-review reason (.github/scripts/threat_review/budget_scan.py patch, head 304-389). The runner rejects repeat run attempts before scanning (budget_runner.py:175-177) and labels incomplete terminal reviews as requiring human review (38-48, 225-228), without relaxing its visible completion predicate.
Integration must examine the new depth_policy.source_depth implementation and the remaining Scanner.call/integrate logic to verify critical-path selection, retained findings, uncertainty propagation and convergence. Workflow evidence must establish workload configuration, trusted checkout/event inputs and final clearance handling; this batch does not establish those contracts. These are material coverage limits, not proof of a vulnerability. No supported regression finding is identified in the supplied scope.
